examples.question_text:
Find the percentage change:
(a) $175$ changes to $203$.
(b) $96$ changes to $78$.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=203-175\\&=28\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{28}{175}\times100\\&=16\%\end{align*}$
This is a $16\%$ increase.

(b)
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=78-96\\&=-18\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-18}{96}\times100\\&=-18.75\%\end{align*}$
This is an $18.75\%$ decrease.

examples.question_text: A ticket price changes from $\$87$ to $\$52$. Find the percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=52-87\\&=-35\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-35}{87}\times100\\&\approx-40.23\%\end{align*}$
This is a $40.23\%$ decrease, to $2$ decimal places.

examples.question_text:
Find the percentage change when a price of $\$68$ is increased:
(a) to $\$85$
(b) by $\$85$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Increased to $\$85$ gives the final price.
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=85-68\\&=17\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{17}{68}\times100\\&=25\%\end{align*}$
This is a $25\%$ increase.

(b) Increased by $\$85$ gives the change.
$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{85}{68}\times100\\&=125\%\end{align*}$
This is a $125\%$ increase.
The final price is $\$68+\$85=\$153$.

examples.question_text: A price changes from $\$72$ to $\$93$, then back to $\$72$. Find each percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places. Explain why they differ.
examples.solution_text:
From $\$72$ to $\$93$:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=93-72\\&=21\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{21}{72}\times100\\&\approx29.17\%\end{align*}$
This is a $29.17\%$ increase.

From $\$93$ to $\$72$:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=72-93\\&=-21\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-21}{93}\times100\\&\approx-22.58\%\end{align*}$
This is a $22.58\%$ decrease.
The change amount has the same size, but the original amount is different for each calculation. This is why the percentages differ.

examples.question_text:
Find the percentage change when a price of $\$80$ is decreased:
(a) by $\$24$
(b) to $\$24$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Decreased by $\$24$ means the change is $-\$24$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-24}{80}\times100\\&=-30\%\end{align*}$
This is a $30\%$ decrease.

(b) Decreased to $\$24$ gives the final price.
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=24-80\\&=-56\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-56}{80}\times100\\&=-70\%\end{align*}$
This is a $70\%$ decrease.
